## Historical audit: H0013

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/hint-codex-experiments/runs/codex_formal_01/codex_formal_01_I_r1/infer_logs/anko-default-function-arguments/turn_1/trajs.json`. Event references below are to its `main_agent` events; offsets are the supplied observation ranges.

**Inferred goal:** Add default function arguments to Anko, apparently including omitted-argument behavior at call time. The original task instructions are not visible, so the precise required semantics are unknown.

| Area | Evidence and finding |
|---|---|
| Autonomous exploration | An attempt to branch from `main` failed with “invalid reference”; the student inspected branches and created `default-arguments` from the detached checkout, whose commit matched `master` (events 1–6, [0,755), [0,349), [0,749), [0,10540), [0,812), [0,1380)). |
| Reproduction | The student wrote a temporary Go program invoking `parser.ParseSrc` on `func f(a = 2) { return a }; f()`; it printed `syntax error`. This validates a parse failure, not runtime default semantics (events 7–8, [0,1071), [0,2346)). |
| Diagnosis | Inspection showed function productions use identifier lists, `FuncExpr` stores parameter names and a variadic flag, and VM calls construct reflection-based functions and check arity (events 12, 14, 18, respectively [0,37508), [0,57805), [0,7869)). The student concluded call-time support needed uncompleted changes (event 19, [0,1024)). |
| Changes and outcome | The branch and temporary reproducer were created, but the student reported no implementation or commit and an unchanged working tree (event 19, [0,1024)). Inventory metadata reports a zero-byte patch, **0/2 fail-to-pass and 119/119 pass-to-pass**: formally not solved, despite existing tests passing. This is an empty-patch outcome, not evidence of a failed proposed algorithm. |
| Teacher input | No actual teacher text or delivery is visible; metadata records zero teacher checks and wait time (top-level metadata, [0,2770)). Linked hints and after-round reviews establish availability only, not receipt or adoption. |

**Lessons and uncertainty:** The transferable observation is that a minimal reproduction can identify a failing stage without proving the complete feature or a fix. The identifier-only grammar and reflection arity checks are task-specific findings; whether and how they must change remains an untested hypothesis. No successful default-argument execution, feature tests, or implementation validation is visible. The initial Git error was recovered from, not a terminal technical interruption; the run ended normally (top-level metadata, [0,2770)).
